items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It was educator Leonard Gornes, Donald Byrd, and myself, the three of us interviewed him.

ctx.x: I know we are moving chronologically, but I just wanted to ask you about trumpet players. One of the things that I’ve noticed about your career is how you have stayed in touch and looked out for the older trumpet players. How did you start meeting the ones from other generations? Talk about them.

The trumpet players and the musicians from the other generations? I think that comes from me and my friend Joe Orange. Joe Orange was a trombonist, we worked—I got him with Lionel Hampton, he was with Eddie Palmieri, he worked with numerous people like that. His uncle was J.C. Hickenbottom. We used to go down to the Metropole when J.C. was working there, and we couldn’t go in because we were too young, but we’d stand outside and hear the band play.
